transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, what finally made me call the employee assistance program at work is that I’m... I'm just barely sleeping right. I go to bed and just lie there, replaying stuff from work or arguments from home. And then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I basically start the day feeling like I never really rested at all.

When you are lying awake at night, do you find that you are worrying excessively about a wide range of different topics, such as your work performance, your health, and your finances, almost every day?

No, I wouldn't say it's a wide range of things like my health or money. It's really just... what I mentioned before. I get stuck replaying specific things that happened that day, like a frustrating conversation at work or a disagreement at home. 

I'm not really worrying about everything else, my mind just kind of loops on the stuff that's already bothering me.
Did these sleep difficulties and the focus on these specific distressing events begin after a particular life change or stressful event occurred?
Yeah, I'd say so. It's been going on for about a year and two months now. That's basically right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse.
Beyond the sleep issues and the rumination, have you been feeling significantly down, sad, or have you lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. It's... I guess most days I feel like this heavy, gray mood just follows me around. It's with me at the office, in the car on the commute, and then right into the house. Even on days when nothing specific is going wrong or happening, I just feel kind of hollow.
During this past year, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely like your old self, without this 'heavy, gray mood'?

No, not really. I mean, maybe there's a good day here and there, or a weekend where I'm just distracted enough, but... no, definitely not for two whole months. It hasn't really lifted for any long stretch like that since this all started.
Besides feeling down and having trouble sleeping, have you been experiencing a persistent sense of low energy or fatigue throughout the day?

No, not really. I mean, obviously I'm a bit tired sometimes if I had a bad night of sleep, but... I wouldn't say I have low energy or fatigue all day. My energy levels are mostly fine. I still get through my work and everything without much of a problem. It's really just the mood more than feeling physically drained.
Do you often find yourself feeling hopeless about the future or feeling like you are not good enough?

Yeah, I do. I guess I just feel like I'm not good enough for my family a lot of the time. I keep replaying every late night I've spent at work, every time I've gone to a tailgate instead of being home, every dumb purchase I've made... and I just end up thinking my wife and kids got stuck with a selfish guy who just keeps letting them down. It's hard not to feel pretty bad about myself when I look at it all.
When you feel like you aren't good enough, do you find that you are preoccupied with these feelings of worthlessness or excessive, inappropriate guilt almost every day?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it really is an everyday thing. I just get stuck on it. My mind constantly loops through all of it—staying late at the office again, blowing money on stupid things, choosing a tailgate over being home. It's just this daily guilt, you know? I just can't stop thinking about how my wife and kids got stuck with such a selfish guy who just keeps letting them down. So, yeah, I guess I am pretty preoccupied with it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight since this mood started, or have others mentioned that you seem to be moving or speaking much more slowly or restlessly than usual?

I haven't really noticed any changes in how I move or talk, and no one else has brought anything like that up. But as for my appetite... yeah, it's been off for months now. 

I basically just run on coffee all the way through lunch, and then I mostly just pick at my dinner when I sit down with my family. The weird thing is, even with my appetite being like that, I realized recently that my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to. So I guess my weight has gone up a little bit despite not eating normal meals.
Beyond the appetite changes, the guilt, and the sleep issues we've discussed, have you found it difficult to concentrate or make decisions on a regular basis?

Yeah, actually. Work has been getting pretty tough lately because of that. I used to be able to knock out my sales forecasts and client decks pretty quickly. It was just second nature. But lately... I don't know, I'll just sit there and read the same slide like five times. And then I start second-guessing every single number I put down. It takes me forever just to decide what to say or how to present it. It's just really hard to focus and make a call on things right now.
